### Data Cleaning

The goals of this section:

- punctuation

- filler words (ex. oh, ah, er)

- wrong glossing (as in proper nouns labeled as nouns or NAs)

- mixed-language labeling (also names)

```{r}

all_data <- full_join(herring1_cgwords, herring2_cgwords)

#This step removed columns that are composed of entirely NA values. it then summarizes the number of instances each language appears per word.
data <- herring1_cgwords |>
  select(-fix,-eng, -com, -clause, -clauseno) |>
  group_by(langid) |>
  summarize(n())

#The prior step shows that punctuation is coded as 999 under language, which makes it unuseful for the current purpose.

#Remove punctuation and remove the redundant auto gloss repetition of the word.
data_clean <- all_data|>
  select(-fix,-eng, -com, -clause, -clauseno) |>
  filter(langid != "",langid !="999" ) |>
  mutate(auto = if_else(str_detect(auto,"."), str_extract(auto,"(?<=\\.).*"), auto), 
         pos = if_else(str_detect(auto,"."), str_extract(auto,"^[^.]+"), auto)
         ) 

#extract major POS, separate inflections
data_clean <- data_clean |>
  mutate(
    langid = str_replace(langid,"eng&spa", "eng"), # might change to remove
    pos = na_if(pos, ""),
    pos = replace_na(pos, "N"), 
    gender = if_else(str_detect(auto,"\\.(F|M)\\."), str_extract(auto,"(F|M)"), "neuter"), 
    number = if_else(str_detect(auto,"\\.(SG|\\dS|P)"), str_extract(auto,"(SG|\\dS|\\dP)"), "neuter"))

# Joining for superdata on conversations






# test_str <- c("PRON.SUB.F.3S","V.INFIN")
#

# str_extract(test_str ,"\\.(F|M)")

```

### Summary Statistics

Goals:

- determine where switches happen (before and after)

- Spanish use per speaker

- Frequency of code-switch per speaker and part of speech

```{r}
#utterance word length by speaker
data_clean |>
    add_count(speaker, utterance_id) |>
    group_by(speaker) |>
    summarise(avg_sentence = mean(n)) |> # keep until here for avg utternace length
  ggplot(aes(x=avg_sentence)) + # prob remove not that useful
  geom_bar() #remove OSE

#Length of utterance
# ggplot(data_clean, aes(x=utterance_id)) +
#   geom_bar()

#spanish frequency by speaker
data_clean |>
  group_by(speaker) |>
  filter(langid == "spa") |>
  summarize(n())

#POS 1 before switch
boundaries <- data_clean |>
  group_by(speaker, utterance_id) |>
  mutate(
    next_lang = lead(langid), #find the next entry for lang
    next_pos = lead(pos) #next entry for POS
  ) |>
  ungroup() |>
  filter(!is.na(next_lang)) |> #Utterance end filter (speaker change)
  mutate(switch = as.integer(langid != next_lang)) #binary codeswitch

count(boundaries, pos, sort =TRUE)

pos_table <- boundaries |>
  group_by(pos) |>
  summarise(
    boundaries = n(), #how many times that POS appears
    switches   = sum(switch), #switch occurred after POS
    rate       = switches / boundaries,
    .groups = "drop"
  )

overall_rate <- mean(boundaries$switch)


Spk_rate_table <- boundaries |>
  group_by(speaker) |>
  summarise(
    boundaries = n(),
    switches   = sum(switch),
    rate       = switches / boundaries,
    .groups = "drop"
  )



```

## Experimental Eye-Tracking Data

"The current study aimed to assess whether bilinguals similarly use visual cues in the parafovea, such as orthographic form and language status, to anticipate and therefore reduce costs related to the processing of an intra-sentential code-switch"

```{r}
test <- et_data |>
  group_by(cognate_status, code_switch, gender, Masked) |>
  filter(Article == 1|Target == 1, IA_SKIP == 0) |>
  summarize(
    group_mean = mean(as.numeric(IA_FIRST_RUN_DWELL_TIME)),
    SD = sd(as.numeric(IA_FIRST_RUN_DWELL_TIME)),
    n = n(),
    SE =SD/sqrt(n),
    .groups = "drop")
  
ggplot(test, aes(x = code_switch, y = group_mean, fill = Masked)) +
  geom_bar(stat = "identity", position = position_dodge(0.9)) +
             geom_errorbar(
               aes(ymin = group_mean - SE, ymax = group_mean + SE),
               position = position_dodge(0.9),
               width = 0.25                 # Width of the horizontal error bar caps
             ) +
  facet_grid(cognate_status ~ gender) +
  scale_fill_manual( values = c("Y" = "magenta", "N" = "blue")) +
  coord_cartesian(ylim = c(220,NA))
  
  
```
